Update, 10:13 p.m. ET: Apple has confirmed that this launch is for "customers with Visa and Mastercard credit cards issued by Axis Bank." Original story below.

Nearly twelve years after Apple first unveiled Apple Pay, the feature has finally launched in India, making it one of the few major markets that didn't have Apple Pay. Here's what you need to know.

Apple Pay finally expands to India

TechCrunch previously reported that Apple Pay would launch in India "later Tuesday," with Axis Bank as the first banking partner.

Now, as spotted by Aaron Perris on X, Apple has started activating Apple Pay support for India on its servers, indicating a rollout is underway.

According to an Apple support article, Apple Pay is now supported in 101 countries and regions, including India.

India has rapidly become one of Apple's most important strategic countries, both for manufacturing and consumer growth.

In addition to expanding its retail presence and touting strong growth there on multiple quarterly earnings calls, Apple and its suppliers have been moving more iPhone production to India as part of a larger strategy to diversify manufacturing beyond China.

But that expansion hasn't come without controversy. Apple is currently fighting a Competition Commission of India antitrust case regarding its App Store practices, and has refused to comply with a government order that requires smartphone manufacturers to preinstall a government-operated app on new devices.

Apple's manufacturing partner Tata Electronics has also recently come under fire after an Indian pollution regulator accused its iPhone component factory of contaminating groundwater and nearby farmland with wastewater discharge.

Tata was also recently hit with a cyberattack that allegedly leaked confidential documents from companies including Apple.

That said, Apple Pay's launch in India signals yet another step in Apple's broader expansion in the country, and could help its services business at this point in time.

In the previous fiscal quarter, Apple's services revenue declined quarter-over-quarter for the first time since Q4 fiscal year 2022. Of course, India alone is unlikely to turn things around immediately, but with iPhone sales hitting record highs there, Apple Pay gives the company another way to sustain that growth momentum.
